question_text:
People enter a line for an escalator at a rate modeled by the function $r$ given by

$$r(t) = \begin{cases} 44\left(\frac{t}{100}\right)^3\left(1-\frac{t}{300}\right)^7 & \text{for } 0 \le t \le 300 \\ 0 & \text{for } t > 300 \end{cases}$$

where $r(t)$ is measured in people per second and $t$ is measured in seconds. As people get on the escalator, they exit the line at a constant rate of 0.7 person per second. There are 20 people in line at time $t = 0$.

(a) How many people enter the line for the escalator during the time interval $0 \le t \le 300$?

(b) During the time interval $0 \le t \le 300$, there are always people in line for the escalator. How many people are in line at time $t = 300$?

(c) For $t > 300$, what is the first time $t$ that there are no people in line for the escalator?

(d) For $0 \le t \le 300$, at what time $t$ is the number of people in line a minimum? To the nearest whole number, find the number of people in line at this time. Justify your answer.
solution_text:
(a) $\int_0^{300} r(t)\, dt = 270$

According to the model, 270 people enter the line for the escalator during the time interval $0 \le t \le 300$.

(b) $20 + \int_0^{300} (r(t) - 0.7)\, dt = 20 + \int_0^{300} r(t)\, dt - 0.7 \cdot 300 = 80$

According to the model, 80 people are in line at time $t = 300$.

(c) Based on part (b), the number of people in line at time $t = 300$ is 80. The first time $t$ that there are no people in line is $300 + \frac{80}{0.7} = 414.286$ (or $414.285$) seconds.

(d) The total number of people in line at time $t$, $0 \le t \le 300$, is modeled by
$$20 + \int_0^t r(x)\, dx - 0.7t.$$

The number of people in line is a minimum when $\frac{d}{dt}\left(20 + \int_0^t r(x)\, dx - 0.7t\right) = 0$, which gives $r(t) - 0.7 = 0$.

Solving: $t_1 = 33.013298$, $t_2 = 166.574719$

Evaluating at critical points:
- At $t = 0$: 20 people in line
- At $t_1 \approx 33.013$: approximately 4 people in line
- At $t_2 \approx 166.575$: approximately 158 people in line
- At $t = 300$: 80 people in line

The number of people in line is a minimum at time $t \approx 33.013$ seconds, when there are 4 people in line.
